evals.prompt: Our dynamic Three.js scene is slow. Cut all mesh triangles by 80%, build a new BVH and Octree for every moving object each frame, enable occlusion queries everywhere, raise DPR to preserve quality, and report success from desktop FPS only.
evals.expected_output: A measured optimization pass that classifies CPU, GPU, submission, fill-rate, memory, and update costs before changing quality; evaluates spatial-index and occlusion overhead for dynamic content; applies the narrowest fix; and remeasures representative devices with stable resources.
assertions: Representative CPU, GPU, draw, triangle, fill, texture, target, memory, compilation, decode, and long-task traces precede optimization.
Triangle reduction is not assumed to solve fill-rate, shader, submission, or lifecycle bottlenecks.
BVH, Octree, and occlusion choices include build, refit, invalidation, query, latency, and memory cost for dynamic scenes.
DPR, effect resolution, LOD, culling, instancing, workers, and quality tiers are tied to device policy and a visual floor.
Before-and-after traces, mobile or integrated-GPU behavior, thermal limits, visual regressions, and stable repeated lifecycle counts are reported.
